h: Seeing the Land Before Taking Possession

p: "See, I have set the land before you;
It opens with "See" in the singular,
and afterward "before you" in the plural,
Also, in this whole matter, it says
"See, I have set" in the past tense,
and likewise "has set" in the past tense,
and in the wilderness, where you saw
"before your eyes," in the plural, "you saw," in the singular
first it speaks in the plural
of these men shall see," etc.,
and to him I will give the land," etc.
It is difficult: why does it mention
"and to him I will give the land,"
and the two hundred includes the hundred?
גַּם אַחַר כָּךְ כְּתִיב בַּפָּרָשָׁה (שָׁם ב, כד)
Also, afterward it is written in the parshah (Devarim 2:24):
"See, I have given into your hand
what is the precision of the word "See"?
it is written "I have given," in the past tense,
"begin to possess it, and provoke him to war,"
וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּתִיב גַּם כֵּן (שָׁם ב, לא)
And afterward it is also written (Devarim 2:31):
"See, I have begun to deliver before you
on what is said in Parshas Pinchas
"And he shall stand before Elazar the Kohen," etc.:
the power would enter into Yehoshua
which is the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
which every one of Yisrael has as his portion.
For by the power of Elazar's seeing
and this is what is said there:
"at his word they shall go out,
and at his word they shall come in"
מָצִינוּ בְּרֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת רְאֵה (דְּבָרִים יא, כו)
we find at the beginning of Parshas Re'eh (Devarim 11:26),
it opens with "See" in the singular
וְאָמְרוּ מֵרַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה
And they said in the name of our holy Rebbe, of blessed memory,
is before every one of Yisrael,
while the seeing is handed over
and this is why it says "See" in the singular,
"I set before you" in the plural
And according to our approach it may be
to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
to bring in through his seeing
he was able to take vengeance on Hashem's enemies,
and also to repair everything at the root.
וְזֶה הַכֹּחַ מָסַר אַחַר כָּךְ לְאֶלְעָזָר
And this power he later handed over to Elazar,
"The honor does not depart from your father's house"
(as is written in the Sifrei on Pinchas)
(בַּמִּדְבַּר רַבָּה כא, טו; תַּנְחוּמָא פִּנְחָס יא)
And this is why it says "See, I — Anochi":
and this is the power of seeing
and this is handed over only to select individuals.
is handed over only to select individuals;
and through the power of seeing,
"I have set the land before you."
in which every one of Yisrael
but through the seeing of the individual
the light "that it was good" enters
"And he shall stand before Elazar the Kohen."
And it says "Come and possess the land":
after the seeing of the individual was effective
and to attain the power of the holiness of Eretz Yisrael,
which is the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh
עַל יְדֵי זֶה בֹּאוּ וּרְשׁוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ
through this, "come and possess the land
which Hashem swore to your fathers,
to Avraham, to Yitzchak and to Yaakov,
and to their seed after them."
and what does it come to teach
with 'to Avraham, to Yitzchak and to Yaakov'?
Avraham is worthy in his own right,
Yitzchak is worthy in his own right,
Yaakov is worthy in his own right."
is the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א מז, ב)
for Shabbos is the middah of Malchus,
we call it Torah she'b'al peh
And it is stated in the holy Zohar
is the secret of the three Avos, etc.,
and the 'bas,' daughter, is crowned with them."
And the power of Torah she'b'al peh
is to break the yetzer hara
and to repair the "abundance of anger";
and on this account he is called Yisrael,
"for you have striven with God and with men";
and that means Torah she'b'al peh.

p: is on account of his offspring,
and they can conquer the yetzer hara
(as is written in the Midrash Rabbah
רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תּוֹלְדוֹת, בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סג, ג)
at the beginning of Parshas Toldos, Bereishis Rabbah 63:3);
that is, after Yaakov was born,
are not counted as his seed
And this is what it says:
"Avraham is worthy in his own right,
Yitzchak is worthy in his own right"
(as is written in the Midrash Rabbah there)
"Yaakov is worthy in his own right"
for he attained the level of truth:
וּשְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד (מִשְׁלֵי יב, יט)
and "the lip of truth shall be established forever" (Mishlei 12:19).
And this is why it says
"to give to them and to their seed after them":
the holiness of the three Avos,
and this is the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
And this was said at Chorev,
as is written in the holy Zohar
and I said to you, You have come," etc.,
Here too it is written "See, He has set,"
that He set the land before you.
And it is written "Hashem your God,"
as at the Giving of the Torah:
and it is like what is said
at the beginning of Parshas Re'eh:
And this was said to the individual,
to whom the power of seeing was handed over,
to bring in the light "that it was good,"
and to attain the holiness of the land,
which is from the "dew of Atika."
אַךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר כָּאן אַחַר כָּךְ
But what is said here afterward
as Hashem, the God of your fathers,
הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ
it is according to what is said afterward:
"Hashem your God who goes before you,
just as He did for you
the whole pasuk is written in the plural;
"and in the wilderness, where you saw
"in all the way that you went," etc.
that the way was not the same for all of them;
And according to our approach it may be
that in Egypt all Yisrael merited
and likewise afterward at the Giving of the Torah,
as we cited from the holy Zohar.
And this is why it says
that they all merited to see.
and the seeing of all was not equal.
And this is why it says:
how Hashem your God carried you,
for each one saw according to his level:
and some at a level lower than that.
And so is the matter here
again it is written in the singular,
even regarding the inheritance of the land:
as Hashem, the God of your fathers,
according to his level and his root.
"Do not fear and do not be dismayed":
do not fear the yetzer hara,
that it will not let you
and do not be dismayed by the past;
is the counsel to break the yetzer hara,
and also to repair the past,
וְזֶה הָעִנְיָן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ
And this is the matter of what is said afterward:
"Not one man of these men shall see," etc.
that they will not merit seeing at all;
that he will merit the distinction of seeing,
and through this he will be able
and "to him I will give the land"
that there be fixed in the heart for generations
the holiness of Torah she'b'al peh.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ (שָׁם א, לח)
And this is what is said afterward (Devarim 1:38):
for this power Moshe Rabbeinu handed over
in that he brought into him the light "that it was good,"
"he shall cause Yisrael to inherit it"
that he would apportion to each and every one of Yisrael
for this is the essence of the division of the land,
"for it is the arrangement of Eretz Yisrael."
And afterward the power of seeing was handed over
"And he shall stand before Elazar the Kohen," etc.,
"at his word they shall go out,
and at his word they shall come in."
For after the sending of the spies,
the power of seeing was handed over
and this is handed over to all Yisrael.
And this is what is said afterward:
"See, I have given into your hand
"I have given," in the past tense,
to conquer the kelipah of Sichon;
for afterward there is need of
for the war against the yetzer hara,
and in its plain sense, for the conquest of the land.
And in the Baal HaTurim he wrote:
And the intent is also as stated:
so that his hand and power would be bound,
in order that they could conquer him.
"See, I have begun to deliver before you
and made him tread on his neck."
And this is in the manner of what we said
"The tzaddik will rejoice when he sees vengeance,"
שֶׁנִּדְרָשׁ (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה מַטּוֹת, בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה כב, ה)
which is expounded (Midrash Rabbah Matos, Bamidbar Rabbah 22:5)
"he will wash his feet in the blood of the wicked."
And we said that through the seeing
he merited to repair everything down to the root:
even what a person tramples with his heels.
"begin to possess, to inherit his land"
meaning to extract everything from Sichon,
even the root of the kelipah;
that is, the root of the kelipah,
which still remains dwelling, in the present,
And this Moshe Rabbeinu himself smote,
and he handed over the power to all Yisrael
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and this is through the power of Torah she'b'al peh.
As it says regarding the seven nations:
"You shall not let any soul live"
to uproot the entire kelipah from the root.
And regarding Sichon this power was
